query: For high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles intended for catalysis, sensing, energy storage, corrosion-related uses, and other applications requiring thermal stability, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs their premelting and melting behavior and why? Specify a controlled comparison that would reveal the governing factor, the observations expected relative to a baseline, the range over which the hypothesis should hold, prior evidence that supports it, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: For equiatomic face-centered-cubic high-entropy-alloy (HEA) nanoparticles in the 5–20 nm size range, the variance of the constituent elements’ surface energies (γvariance) is the primary factor governing the onset of premelting and the overall melting temperature (Tm,np). A higher γvariance promotes thermally activated surface segregation that locally lowers the solidus (forming low-melting surface regions), so nanoparticles whose element set has a large γvariance will exhibit earlier premelting and a larger depression of Tm,np than compositionally similar particles whose elements have nearly equal surface energies.
generation.material_initial_state: Quasi-equiatomic 5-element FCC HEA nanoparticles, 10 ± 2 nm in diameter, synthesized by inert-gas condensation and collected as oxide-free powders.
generation.intervention: Systematically replace one or two elements to create two compositions with (i) low γvariance (e.g., CoNiFeCuPd) and (ii) high γvariance (e.g., CoNiFeCuAg), while keeping mean cohesive energy, crystal structure and particle size distribution the same.
generation.conditions: Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) and in-situ TEM heating under high vacuum (≤10⁻⁶ Torr) with a 10 K min⁻¹ ramp from 300 K to 1500 K.
generation.structural_mediator: Extent of thermally induced surface segregation, quantified by in-situ STEM-EDS line profiles and atom-probe tomography after quench.
generation.mechanism: Large element-to-element surface energy contrasts lower the Gibbs free energy cost of segregation. Segregated surface patches are compositionally biased toward low-melting constituents, nucleating surface premelting and accelerating whole-particle melting once a percolating liquid shell forms.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the low-γvariance baseline HEA, the high-γvariance HEA nanoparticles will (i) show the first detectable DSC premelting endotherm and onset of surface roughening in TEM ≥100 K earlier, and (ii) exhibit a 50–150 K lower peak melting temperature. The difference should scale monotonically with γvariance across a series of compositions.
generation.baseline: Low-γvariance HEA nanoparticles (CoNiFeCuPd) with confirmed near-random atomic distribution and no pre-existing segregation.
generation.boundary: Particle diameters 5–20 nm; FCC solid solution; heating in inert or high-vacuum environments; ramp rates ≤20 K min⁻¹. Outside this range (e.g., larger particles where surface/volume ratio is small or BCC structures) the correlation may weaken.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of the temperature shifts (100 ± 50 K) is estimated; actual values may vary with synthesis defects or oxide contamination. If hidden ordered phases form, they could mask the effect.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two HEA nanoparticle batches differing only in γvariance as described. Perform identical DSC and in-situ TEM heating while monitoring (a) heat flow, (b) real-time morphology, and (c) surface composition profiles before and after heating.
measurements: Onset temperature of first DSC endotherm (premelting)
Temperature of first observable surface roughening in TEM
Surface composition gradients (surface/core concentration ratio) at multiple temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if the high-γvariance HEA does NOT display (i) an earlier premelting onset and lower Tm,np than the low-γvariance HEA, or (ii) measurably greater surface segregation prior to premelting; or if the trend of Tm,np with γvariance is non-monotonic across at least three compositions.
